newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Yamaichi to close London futures ops.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Yamaichi to close London futures ops.

text.p: Yamaichi International (Europe) said on Thursday it planned to close its futures and options section in London over the next month, a move LIFFE traders said partly reflected tougher competition among brokerages and shrinking margins.
The move by the Japanese firm, which is in the middle of a restructuring programme, affected 15 staff on the floor of LIFFE and on the bank's sales desk, Yamaichi said.
One trader at a London bank said a commission price war among brokers on LIFFE keen to attract business meant margins were suffering.

"There's an ongoing trend of increased competition and commissions have got squeezed," he said. "There may be some more houses to follow, but it won't be an onslaught because most of the houses which are weak enough to fall have already gone."
The trader noted there had not been an increase in the number of houses touting for business, rather volume of trade had been moderate.

"The remaining houses are desperately trying to increase their volumes. I don't think volumes have been amazing in the second quarter compared to the first quarter of this year, so people are reacting by cutting their margins to try and get more business in that way," he said.
Yamaichi said in a statement it could not justify the large amounts of capital needed to remain competitive in this market.

"Yamaichi has seats on the floor of LIFFE and a small sales and trading desk in its office on Finsbury Pavement and plans to wind down its F&O (futures and options) business over the next month," the bank said.

"Over the last two years, Yamaichi has successfully expanded its F&O operations. However, although the section is profitable, the company feels that to become a major player in this market would require large amounts of capital which could be utilised more effectively in other parts of its business," the bank said.
A spokesperson at LIFFE said Yamaichi would continue to be a general clearing member of LIFFE and would retain its clearing function for proprietary business.
Thursday's announcement follows closely on news of a downgrade by rating agency Standard & Poor's on June 5.

S&P downgraded Yamaichi Securuties' long-term counterparty rating to BBB from BBB plus, citing the bank's prolonged poor performance and an expected negative impact from ongoing deregulation in the Japanese securities industry.
But the agency also revised the outlook to stable from negative and said this was because of restructuring efforts already in progress.

Santi Kalf, head of bond trading at Yamaichi, said in the statement: "With falling margins, it is our view that we cannot justify the major investment of capital needed to remain competitive in this market in the future."
